title: ReAIM: A ReRAM-based Adaptive Ising Machine for Solving Combinatorial Optimization Problems
problem: Ising Machines solving NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems face the von Neumann bottleneck from frequent data transfers between compute and memory. Existing ReRAM-based Ising Machine accelerators struggle with non-ideal device characteristics and limited algorithm flexibility.
motivation: Ising Machines efficiently solve NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems across multiple domains, but hardware implementations are hindered by the von Neumann bottleneck and device non-idealities.
method: ReAIM puts computation directly inside memory using ReRAM (resistive memory that stores data by changing electrical resistance), avoiding the slow back-and-forth movement of data between computer and memory. Since real ReRAM devices don't work perfectly, ReAIM uses an adaptive algorithm that automatically selects the best solver method and settings by accounting for both software factors (which algorithm to use, how many spin flip steps to attempt) and hardware realities (how the ReRAM devices actually behave). This flexibility comes from a reconfigurable design that can efficiently map and schedule computations for different problems.
key_novelty: The innovation is an adaptive algorithm that automatically finds and applies the best solver method and settings for each problem by accounting for both software choices and the real-world imperfections of ReRAM hardware.
contributions: ReRAM-based Processing-in-Memory architecture for Ising Machine acceleration
Adaptive parameter search algorithm for dynamic solver and configuration selection
Reconfigurable hardware design with optimized mapping and scheduling strategies
2.2× speedup over SRAM-based IM accelerators without compromising solution quality
